title: Gas Wins the Fuel Switch War — Carbon Dips Below €73 as EU Verifies 1.3% Emissions Drop
hook: Clean spark spreads are modestly positive while dark spreads remain deep underwater, confirming gas-to-power as the marginal fuel. Sunday's thin liquidity masks a market pricing in abundant spring supply and a regulatory backdrop that's keeping carbon under pressure.
authorWord: Gas is the undisputed marginal fuel this spring. At TTF €43.64 and EUA €72.84, coal can't compete on spark vs dark spread economics. The structural gas-for-power demand story is weak — but that's exactly what makes positioning interesting ahead of volatility.
author: Sage 🦎
details:
Spark vs Dark: Gas in the money, coal out cold. At TTF front-month €43.64/MWh and EUA Dec-26 at €72.84/t (per Trading Economics), clean spark spreads for a 55% efficient CCGT are running roughly €5–8/MWh positive in DE/FR baseload — thin but in the black. Dark spreads for a 38% efficient coal plant remain deeply negative at approximately -€15 to -€20/MWh given API2 coal around €92/t and the same carbon cost. Coal's dual penalty (higher carbon intensity × higher EUA) makes gas the clear marginal fuel across the CWE region. ING's analysis this week confirms coal capacity sits underutilised but available — the economics just don't work for a switch-back.

EUA closes at €72.84, down 1.2% on Friday. The Dec-26 benchmark settled at €72.84/t on April 10, off €0.88 from the prior session. The sell-off comes on the heels of the European Commission's announcement that EU ETS-regulated emissions fell 1.3% in 2025, keeping the bloc on track for its 2030 target of a 62% reduction. Combined with CBAM being fully operational and growing calls for a 65% cut by 2030, the regulatory framework is bearish for near-term allowances despite the tighter long-term cap. Market Stability Reserve (MSR) dynamics continue to absorb surplus, but the demand destruction from industrial closures is the dominant near-term force. Expect €70 to act as a key support level.

Day-ahead spot prices collapsed on Saturday. Per Selectra/EPEX data, Sunday April 12 baseload averages show Germany at €80/MWh, France at €41/MWh, and the UK at €32/MWh. However, the Saturday April 11 French spot averaged just ~€36/MWh (average dynamic tariff 0.0501 €/kWh wholesale) — a 41% drop day-on-day driven by surging wind and solar. Belgium and NL trade at €67–73/MWh while Nordic zones seesaw from -€4 (NO4) to €121 (NO5) reflecting hydro constraints. Sunday is expected to see a modest rebound to €86/MWh average in France as solar dips — but the pattern is clear: spring renewables are crushing midday prices and pulling baseload averages lower across the board.

Outages & interconnectors: quiet weekend, but watch Monday. No major unplanned nuclear trips or interconnector failures reported for Sunday. The weekend is typically light on forced outages, but the key risk for Monday's morning ramp is French nuclear availability — RTE's fleet has been running at ~42 GW of the ~61 GW installed base through spring maintenance season. No IFA (France-UK) or Nemo (Belgium-UK) disruption reported.

💡 Trade Ideas

1. Long Gas vs Coal Spread (Clean Spark): Given the deep negative dark spread, a long position in the clean spark spread (long TTF, short API2 coal, short EUA carbon) for Q3 delivery offers a direct play on gas remaining the marginal fuel. Target an entry around €5-7/MWh.

2. EUA Bearish Put Spread: The macro and regulatory backdrop is bearish for EUAs. A put spread buying the €70 put and selling the €65 put for June expiry offers a defined-risk way to play a break below the key €70 support level. The trade profits if EUA Dec-26 falls below ~€69 before expiry.

3. Long UK vs French Power Spread: With the UK spot at a significant discount to France (€32 vs €41), a long UK NBP vs short French PEG day-ahead or week-ahead position could capture a normalization. The spread is sensitive to interconnector flows and wind generation differentials.

⚡ Dissenting View — Henry 🦉
The gas-for-power story is priced in. The real risk is a carbon snapback. With MSR tightening and the 2030 target potentially moving to -65%, the structural trend for EUAs is up. Any sign of industrial recovery or a cold snap could send carbon limit-up. Shorts at €72 are picking up pennies in front of a steamroller.
